extracted.intended_audience: novelists, literary critics, and students of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for shaping the form and method of a novel: choices about time, space, point of view, selection of material, and consistent method to produce a unified artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illumination/contrast to reveal inner life
rubrics_metrics.description: The illumination that falls upon his page is like the glare of a furnace-mouth; it searches the depths of the inner struggles and turmoils in which his drama is enacted, relieving it with sharp and fantastic shadows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ lighting/contrast (literal or figurative) to isolate and intensify characters' inner consciousness; remove surrounding 'natural day' so the focus is on inner theatre. Example: Dostoevsky’s dramatic glare and thick curtain of darkness that make inner turmoil visible. Anti-pattern: diffuse or even lighting that flattens psychological intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of space and daylight (creating large vision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuity of space and of daylight, so necessary to the motive of the book, is rendered in War and Peace with absolute mastery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an uninterrupted sense of physical space and daylight to give the reader an expansive, open world. This contributes to a feeling that the novel's characters inhabit a larger world beyond the pages. Not achieved merely by multiplying names or descriptions, but by authorial technique that allows freedom of movement and latitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey a world beyond the characters (freedom/latitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: He manages to give them such freedom, such an obvious latitude of movement in the open world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters feel as if their lives continue beyond the book's bounds by treating them as if they have independent existence; avoid over-constraining them to the author's narrow stage. Contrast with authors whose detailed habitation makes characters feel confined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use description sparingly where unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Description has nothing to do with it; there is very little description in War and Peace, save in the battle-scenes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on copious description to create scope; sometimes minimal description combined with other techniques (movement, social panorama, continuity) better achieves largeness. Anti-pattern: heavy descriptive passages that substitute for structural methods of creating scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent the passage of time — 'the form of time'
rubrics_metrics.description: The movement of the wheel of time must be made perceptible... The form of time is to be represented, and that is something more than to represent its contents in their order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show time's passage through the book's overall structure: lines and masses, shape and rhythm, not merely by listing events or stating 'years passed.' The novel's form should make the sense of time tangible to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render the double effect of time (lapse + cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The double effect of time — its uninterrupted lapse, and the cycle of which the chosen stretch is a segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the novel displays both steady, silent progression (individual change) and the larger cyclical rise-and-fall (generational sweep). Both aspects should be perceptible when time is central to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a short chronological span feel like a large sweep
rubrics_metrics.description: It must seem to turn in a large circumference, though only a part of its journey is to be watched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the plot covers only years rather than decades, shape the narrative so readers sense a wide circumference of life (e.g., the revolution of a generation). Use motifs, foreshadowing, and character relations to imply the larger sweep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character consistency through change and aging
rubrics_metrics.description: They grow as we all do, they change in the only possible direction, that which results from the clash between themselves and their conditions... their mutability never hides their sameness, their consistency shows and endures through their disintegration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray aging and development realistically while preserving an underlying identity; changes should arise from character interacting with circumstances, not arbitrary shifts. Anti-pattern: characters who change without psychological continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and unity of purpose (the moral/design must be evident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Without design the scattered scenes will make no picture... Our answer would be clear enough... if we could see in the form of the novel an image of the circling sweep of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a controlling design or image that unites scenes and chapters into a coherent whole; the form should announce the reason for the collocation of parts. Avoid merely picturesque or episodic accumulation that fails to cohere into a discernible purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a fixed subject or purpose while writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither his subject nor his method were fixed for him as he wrote; he ranged around his mountain of material, attacking it now here and now there, never deciding in his mind to what end he had amassed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide (and keep) the central subject and method for the work; wandering without a sustained purpose can waste material and weaken the overall effect. Anti-pattern: continual vacillation of aim that leaves threads unfinished and energy dissipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economize material — avoid wasting life that doesn't serve the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: At any moment great masses of that life are being wasted, turned to no account; and the result is... the wasted life... is dividing and weakening the effect of the picture created out of the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cull or reshape episodes and details that do not advance the novel's subject or design. Excess material, even if vivid, can dilute the primary artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix the subject clearly before treatment (Flaubert's example)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Bovary... the subject stands firm and clear, without the least shade of ambiguity to break the line which bounds it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clearly defined subject enables precise choice of method and allows the critic (and reader) to trace the novel's treatment without missing links. Use a settled subject to guide narrative choices instead of discovering the subject as you write.

rubrics_metrics.name: The novel should be an image not a row of facts — show rather than merely tell
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is not a row of facts, it is a single image; the facts have no validity in themselves, they are nothing until they have been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange and shape facts so they cohere into an overall image or impression. Avoid presenting the 'argument' or bare sequence of events as if that alone constituted the art of fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate selection of information and authorial method
rubrics_metrics.description: We are simply concerned with the method by which he selects the information he offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consciously choose what to reveal and by what means (scene, summary, interior access, authorial exposition). Selection determines the reader's relation to the story and shapes its meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic vs panoramic presentation — choose your narrative stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are we placed before a particular scene... Or are we surveying their lives from a height, participating in the privilege of the novelist—sweeping their history with a wide range of vision and absorbing a general effect?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide when to present intimate, scene-by-scene immediacy (scenic) and when to step back for broad summary or panorama. Recognize that shifting from one to the other changes the reader’s engagement and the kinds of truth conveyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial presence and 'impersonality' — handling the writer's voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The famous 'impersonality' of Flaubert... lies only in the greater tact with which they express their feelings—dramatizing them, embodying them in living form, instead of stating them directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide how openly the author's judgements will register. Even 'impersonal' narration conveys opinion via method and phrasing; dramatize evaluative stance through scenes and characterization rather than blunt assertion, unless deliberate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view shifts: authorial omniscience vs character consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: There comes a juncture... it is necessary for us to know more than we could have made out by simply looking and listening... the author... enters their consciousness, and describes the train of sentiment that passes there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authorial intervention to supply background, motivations, or interior life when the scene itself cannot convey what is needed. Conversely, render aspects through a character's perception when you want the world to be colored by that consciousness. Ensure shifts are justified and coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial (mood-coloured) vs dramatic (objective) treatment of scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a pictorial manner of treating the matter in hand and there is also a dramatic... The thing is 'scenic'... but there it is all bathed in the climate of Emma’s mood... The scene is pictorially treated... [versus] a scene which might be put upon the stage... treated dramatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to present a scene primarily through the mood and internal coloration of a character (pictorial) or through outward action and dialogue (dramatic). Each yields different effects: pictorial deepens psychological impression; dramatic foregrounds objective facts and irony. Mixing is possible but must be controlled by the novel's plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix methods judiciously but be consistent on a governing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: He will do both... The only law that binds him throughout... is the need to be consistent on some plan, to follow the principle he has adopted; and of course it is one of the first of his precepts... to allow himself no more latitude than he requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A novel may employ varied devices (scenic/panoramic, pictorial/dramatic, authorial/character POV) but these choices should cohere under an explicit or implicit organizing principle tied to the subject. Vary technique where it serves the design, but avoid random or excessive liberties that break unity.
